<script type="application/json" id="pack-y1w10">{"year":1,"week":10,"id":"y1w10","title":"Perfect Squares and Algebraic Fractions","subtitle":"Square numbers and perfect-square expressions; the difference of two squares; factorising quadratics; simplifying, adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing algebraic fractions with their excluded values.","family":"algebra","section":{"no":2,"name":"Algebra","strand":"Algebraic Reasoning","from":9,"to":12},"outcomes":["Recognise square numbers and perfect-square expressions, and expand $(a\\pm b)^2$.","Explain the difference of two squares with a diagram and use it to factorise.","Factorise quadratic expressions of the form $x^2+bx+c$.","State the excluded values of an algebraic fraction before cancelling.","Simplify, add, subtract, multiply and divide algebraic fractions."],"keywords":["square number","perfect square","difference of two squares","quadratic","algebraic fraction","excluded value","common denominator","reciprocal"],"notes":[{"title":"Square numbers","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A **square number** is an integer multiplied by itself: $1,\\ 4,\\ 9,\\ 16,\\ 25,\\ 36,\\ \\ldots$ A square of side 5 units has an area of $5^2=25$ square units."},{"k":"p","text":"Adding consecutive odd numbers always gives a square number:"},{"k":"fig","id":"w10-odd","caption":"Each odd number adds an L-shaped border to the previous square, so $1+3+5+\\cdots+(2n-1)=n^2$."},{"k":"box","kind":"key","title":"Sum of the first $n$ odd numbers","blocks":[{"k":"math","tex":"1+3+5+\\cdots+(2n-1)=n^2"},{"k":"p","text":"For example, the first 10 odd numbers add up to $10^2=100$."}]}],"figs":["w10-odd"]},{"title":"Squaring a sum or a difference","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A **perfect square** expression is the square of a whole bracket. To square a bracket, multiply it by itself: every term in the first bracket multiplies every term in the second."},{"k":"fig","id":"w10-square","caption":"The square of side $a+b$ is made of $a^2$, two rectangles $ab$ and $b^2$."},{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"Perfect squares","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["$(a+b)^2=a^2+2ab+b^2$","$(a-b)^2=a^2-2ab+b^2$"]}]},{"k":"p","text":"For example, $(2x-3)^2=(2x)^2-2(2x)(3)+3^2=4x^2-12x+9$."},{"k":"box","kind":"warn","title":"$(a+b)^2$ is not $a^2+b^2$","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"The middle term $2ab$ comes from the two cross-products. With $a=3$ and $b=2$: $(3+2)^2=25$, but $3^2+2^2=13$."}]}],"figs":["w10-square"]},{"title":"The difference of two squares","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Start with a square of area $a^2$ and cut away a smaller square of area $b^2$ from one corner. The L-shape that is left can be cut into two rectangles and rearranged into one rectangle $a+b$ long and $a-b$ wide."},{"k":"fig","id":"w10-dos","caption":"The areas are equal, so $a^2-b^2=(a+b)(a-b)$."},{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"Difference of two squares","blocks":[{"k":"math","tex":"a^2-b^2=(a-b)(a+b)"}]},{"k":"ul","items":["$9x^2-25=(3x)^2-5^2=(3x-5)(3x+5)$","$4x^2-36=4(x^2-9)=4(x-3)(x+3)$ (take out the common factor first)","$49-36=7^2-6^2=(7-6)(7+6)=13$"]},{"k":"box","kind":"warn","title":"It must be a difference","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"The sign between the squares must be **minus**. A sum such as $x^2+9$ does not factorise into real brackets this way."}]}],"figs":["w10-dos"]},{"title":"Factorising $x^2+bx+c$","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Expanding $(x+2)(x+3)$ gives $x^2+5x+6$. To reverse this, look for two numbers that **multiply** to give $c=6$ and **add** to give $b=5$: they are $2$ and $3$."},{"k":"fig","id":"w10-trinomial","caption":"The four parts of $x^2+5x+6$ fit together into a rectangle $(x+2)$ by $(x+3)$."},{"k":"table","head":["Expression","Two numbers","Factors"],"rows":[["$x^2+5x+6$","$2,\\ 3$","$(x+2)(x+3)$"],["$x^2-5x+6$","$-2,\\ -3$","$(x-2)(x-3)$"],["$x^2-x-6$","$2,\\ -3$","$(x+2)(x-3)$"],["$x^2+7x+12$","$3,\\ 4$","$(x+3)(x+4)$"]]},{"k":"p","text":"Always check by expanding your answer."}],"figs":["w10-trinomial"]},{"title":"Algebraic fractions and excluded values","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"An **algebraic fraction** has a variable in its numerator or denominator, such as $\\dfrac{x+1}{2x}$ or $\\dfrac{3}{x-5}$. The numerator and the denominator are each complete expressions."},{"k":"box","kind":"definition","title":"Excluded values","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A denominator can **never** be zero. The values of the variable that make the denominator zero are **excluded values**; state them before you simplify."},{"k":"ul","items":["$\\dfrac{x+1}{2x}$: $\\;x\\neq0$","$\\dfrac{3}{x-5}$: $\\;x\\neq5$","$\\dfrac{x-2}{x^2-4}=\\dfrac{x-2}{(x-2)(x+2)}$: $\\;x\\neq2$ and $x\\neq-2$"]}]},{"k":"fig","id":"w10-excluded","caption":"For $\\frac{x^2-9}{x^2+5x+6}$ the denominator $(x+2)(x+3)$ is zero at $x=-2$ and $x=-3$, so these two values are excluded."},{"k":"box","kind":"key","title":"Zero or undefined?","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A fraction is **zero** when its numerator is zero **and** its denominator is not zero. It is **undefined** when its denominator is zero."}]}],"figs":["w10-excluded"]},{"title":"Simplifying: cancel factors, not terms","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"To simplify, factorise the numerator and the denominator completely, then cancel **common factors**:"},{"k":"math","tex":"\\frac{(x-2)(x+3)}{(x-2)(x-5)}=\\frac{x+3}{x-5},\\qquad x\\neq2,\\ 5"},{"k":"box","kind":"warn","title":"Never cancel terms","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"In $\\dfrac{x+2}{x+5}$ the $x$ is a **term** in a sum, not a factor of the whole numerator, so it cannot be cancelled. The excluded values of the original fraction still apply after cancelling: $x\\neq2$ above, even though $(x-2)$ has disappeared."}]}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Adding and subtracting algebraic fractions","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"As with number fractions, you need a **common denominator**. Denominator: $(x-2)(x+2)$.","Undefined where the denominator is zero: $x=2$ or $x=-2$.","Zero where the numerator is zero: $x=2$ or $x=3$.","Reject $x=2$, because $F$ is undefined <script type="application/json" id="pack-y1w11">{"year":1,"week":11,"id":"y1w11","title":"Formulae, Linear Equations and Inequalities","subtitle":"Writing and rearranging formulae; solving linear equations with brackets and fractions; simultaneous equations; solving linear inequalities and showing them on a number line.","family":"algebra","section":{"no":2,"name":"Algebra","strand":"Algebraic Reasoning","from":9,"to":12},"outcomes":["Write formulae from everyday situations and change the subject of a formula.","Solve linear equations with brackets and fractions, and check the solutions.","Solve a pair of simultaneous linear equations by elimination and by substitution.","Solve linear inequalities, reversing the sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative number.","Show solution sets on a number line and interpret answers in context."],"keywords":["expression","equation","formula","subject","inverse operation","linear equation","simultaneous equations","elimination","substitution","inequality","number line"],"notes":[{"title":"Expressions, equations and formulae","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["An **expression** has no equals sign: $3x+7$.","An **equation** states that two expressions are equal: $3x+7=25$.","A **formula** is an equation connecting two or more named quantities, for example $P=2(l+b)\\qquad d=vt\\qquad A=\\tfrac{1}{2}bh$"]},{"k":"p","text":"The **subject** of a formula is the variable on its own on one side; in $d=vt$ the subject is $d$."}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Solving equations: keep the balance","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"An equation is like a balanced scale. Whatever you do to one side, you must do to the other side to keep it balanced."},{"k":"fig","id":"w11-balance","caption":"$3x+7=25$: remove 7 from both pans, then share each pan into 3 equal parts, to find $x=6$."},{"k":"p","text":"Undo the operations in reverse order using **inverse operations**: undo $+$ and $-$ first, then $\\times$ and $\\div$."},{"k":"box","kind":"tip","title":"Always check","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Substitute your answer into the **original** equation. For $3x+7=25$: $3(6)+7=25$ ✓."}]}],"figs":["w11-balance"]},{"title":"Changing the subject of a formula","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"To make a variable the subject, list the operations acting on it, then undo them in reverse order, doing the same to both sides."},{"k":"math","tex":"y=mx+c\\ \\Longrightarrow\\ c=y-mx"},{"k":"math","tex":"A=\\tfrac{1}{2}bh\\ \\Longrightarrow\\ 2A=bh\\ \\Longrightarrow\\ h=\\frac{2A}{b}\\quad(b\\neq0)"},{"k":"math","tex":"E=\\tfrac{1}{2}mv^2\\ \\Longrightarrow\\ v^2=\\frac{2E}{m}\\ \\Longrightarrow\\ v=\\sqrt{\\frac{2E}{m}}\\quad(v\\geq0)"},{"k":"box","kind":"note","title":"Square roots in context","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"When you take a square root, there are two values, $\\pm$. In real situations such as speed or length, keep only the value that makes sense (here $v\\geq0$)."}]}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Equations with brackets","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Expand the brackets carefully (a minus sign outside changes every sign inside), collect the $x$-terms on one side and the numbers on the other."},{"k":"math","tex":"\\begin{aligned}7(x-6)&=3(x+9)\\\\7x-42&=3x+27\\\\4x&=69\\\\x&=\\tfrac{69}{4}\\end{aligned}"}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Equations with fractions","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Multiply **every** term on both sides by the LCM of the denominators. This clears all the fractions at once."},{"k":"math","tex":"\\frac{x}{3}-2=\\frac{1}{2}\\quad\\xrightarrow{\\ \\times6\\ }\\quad2x-12=3\\quad\\Longrightarrow\\quad x=\\frac{15}{2}"},{"k":"box","kind":"warn","title":"Multiply every term","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Do not forget terms with no denominator. In the example above, the $2$ must also be multiplied by $6$ to give $12$."}]}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Simultaneous linear equations","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Two unknowns need two equations. A solution must make **both** equations true at the same time."},{"k":"ul","items":["**Elimination:** add or subtract the equations (after multiplying if necessary) so that one unknown disappears.","**Substitution:** make one unknown the subject of one equation and substitute into the other."]},{"k":"math","tex":"\\begin{aligned}2x+y&=13\\\\x-y&=2\\end{aligned}"},{"k":"p","text":"Adding the equations eliminates $y$: $3x=15$, so $x=5$; then $y=5-2=3$."},{"k":"fig","id":"w11-lines","caption":"Each equation is a straight line. The solution $(5,3)$ is the point where the lines cross."},{"k":"box","kind":"key","title":"Number of solutions","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Two lines that cross give one solution. Parallel lines (same gradient, different intercepts) give **no** solution; two equations for the same line give **infinitely many** solutions."}]}],"figs":["w11-lines"]},{"title":"From words to algebra","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Define the unknown first, with its units. Then translate carefully:"},{"k":"table","head":["Words","Algebra"],"rows":[["five more than twice a number","$2x+5$"],["at least 12","$n\\geq12$"],["no more than 75","$n\\leq75$"],["fewer than 30","$n<30$"],["more than 4","$n>4$"]]},{"k":"p","text":"If $x$ is a number of buses or people, the answer must be a whole number, even though the algebra allows any real number."}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Linear inequalities","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"An **inequality** compares two quantities using $<$, $>$, $\\leq$ or $\\geq$. Solve it like an equation, with one extra rule."},{"k":"box","kind":"warn","title":"The golden rule of inequalities","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"When you **multiply or divide both sides by a negative number**, reverse the inequality sign."},{"k":"math","tex":"-2x>6\\ \\Longrightarrow\\ x<-3"}]},{"k":"fig","id":"w11-flip","caption":"Multiplying by $-1$ reflects numbers in 0, so the order reverses: $2<3$ but $-2>-3$."},{"k":"p","text":"Adding or subtracting any number, or multiplying or dividing by a **positive** number, does not change the direction:"},{"k":"math","tex":"3x+4\\leq19\\ \\Longrightarrow\\ 3x\\leq15\\ \\Longrightarrow\\ x\\leq5"},{"k":"p","text":"On a number line, use an **open circle** for $<$ or $>$ (the endpoint is not included) and a **filled circle** for $\\leq$ or $\\geq$ (the endpoint is included)."},{"k":"fig","id":"w11-inequalities","caption":"Showing solution sets: shade to the left for “less than”, to the right for “greater than”, and between two endpoints for a double inequality."}],"figs":["w11-flip","w11-inequalities"]},{"title":"Checks and common errors","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["$3(x+2)=3x+6$, not $3x+2$.","When clearing fractions, multiply **every** term.","Reverse the sign only when multiplying or dividing by a **negative** number.","Check the answer in the original equation, and ask whether it makes sense (no negative masses or impossible ages)."]}],"figs":[]}],"examples":[{"title":"Changing the subject: perimeter","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"The perimeter of a rectangular classroom is $P=2(l+b)$. Make $b$ the subject, and find $b$ when $P=46$ m and $l=15$ m."}],"steps":["Divide both sides by 2: $\\dfrac{P}{2}=l+b$.","Subtract $l$: $b=\\dfrac{P}{2}-l$.","Substitute: $b=\\dfrac{46}{2}-15=23-15=8$.","Check: $2(15+8)=46$ ✓."],"answer":"$b=\\dfrac{P}{2}-l$; the breadth is 8 m.","figs":[]},{"title":"A formula with a square","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"The kinetic energy of an object is $E=\\tfrac{1}{2}mv^2$. Make $v$ the subject (speed is not negative), then find $v$ when $E=200$ J and $m=4$ kg."}],"steps":["Multiply by 2: $2E=mv^2$.","Divide by $m$ ($m>0$): $v^2=\\dfrac{2E}{m}$.","Take the non-negative square root: $v=\\sqrt{\\dfrac{2E}{m}}$.","Substitute: $v=\\sqrt{\\dfrac{2\\times200}{4}}=\\sqrt{100}=10$."],"answer":"$v=\\sqrt{\\dfrac{2E}{m}}$; the speed is $10$ m/s.","figs":[]},{"title":"Brackets on both sides","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Solve $5(2x-3)-3(x+4)=2x+9$ and check your answer."}],"steps":["Expand: $10x-15-3x-12=2x+9$.","Simplify: $7x-27=2x+9$.","Subtract $2x$ and add $27$: $5x=36$, so $x=\\dfrac{36}{5}$.","Check: left side $=5\\left(\\dfrac{72}{5}-3\\right)-3\\left(\\dfrac{36}{5}+4\\right)=57-\\dfrac{168}{5}=\\dfrac{117}{5}$; right side $=\\dfrac{72}{5}+9=\\dfrac{117}{5}$ ✓."],"answer":"$x=\\dfrac{36}{5}=7.2$","figs":[]},{"title":"An equation with fractions","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Solve $\\dfrac{2x-1}{3}-\\dfrac{x+2}{2}=1$."}],"steps":["The LCM of 3 and 2 is 6. Multiply every term by 6: $2(2x-1)-3(x+2)=6$.","Expand: $4x-2-3x-6=6$.","Simplify: $x-8=6$, so $x=14$.","Check: $\\dfrac{27}{3}-\\dfrac{16}{2}=9-8=1$ ✓."],"answer":"$x=14$","figs":[]},{"title":"Books and pens","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A school bought 18 items, some exercise books at GH₵12 each and some pens at GH₵4 each. The total cost was GH₵152. How many of each did it buy?"}],"steps":["Let $x$ be the number of books and $y$ the number of pens.","Number of items: $x+y=18$. Cost: $12x+4y=152$, which simplifies to $3x+y=38$.","Subtract: $(3x+y)-(x+y)=38-18$, so $2x=20$ and $x=10$.","Then $y=18-10=8$.","Check: $10(12)+8(4)=120+32=152$ ✓."],"answer":"10 exercise books and 8 pens","figs":[]},{"title":"Solving an inequality","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Solve $4-3(2x-1)\\geq2x+15$ and show the solution on a number line."}],"steps":["Expand: $4-6x+3\\geq2x+15$, so $7-6x\\geq2x+15$.","Subtract $2x$ and $7$: $-8x\\geq8$.","Divide by $-8$ and **reverse** the sign: $x\\leq-1$.","Number line: a filled circle at $-1$, shaded to the left (see the first line in the figure above)."],"answer":"$x\\leq-1$","figs":[]},{"title":"How far can Ama travel?","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A delivery service charges GH₵8 plus GH₵3 per kilometre. Ama has GH₵41. Write and solve an inequality for the greatest distance she can pay for."}],"steps":["Let $d$ be the distance in km ($d\\geq0$). The charge is $8+3d$ cedis.","She can spend no more than GH₵41: $8+3d\\leq41$.","Subtract 8: $3d\\leq33$. Divide by 3: $d\\leq11$.","Together with $d\\geq0$: $0\\leq d\\leq11$."],"answer":"At most 11 km.","figs":[]},{"title":"An inequality with fractions","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Solve $\\dfrac{x}{2}-\\dfrac{x+4}{3}>\\dfrac{2x-1}{6}$."}],"steps":["Multiply every term by 6 (positive, so the sign stays): $3x-2(x+4)>2x-1$.","Expand: $3x-2x-8>2x-1$, so $x-8>2x-1$.","Subtract $x$ and add 1: $-7>x$, that is, $x<-7$.","Number line: an open circle at $-7$, shaded to the left."],"answer":"$x<-7$","figs":[]}],"summary":[{"title":"Key results for Week 11","items":["Do the same to both sides; undo operations in reverse order.","To clear fractions, multiply **every** term by the LCM of the denominators.","Simultaneous equations: eliminate one unknown, or substitute.","Multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number reverses the sign.","Open circle for $<,\\ >$; filled circle for $\\leq,\\ \\geq$."]}],"quiz":[{"q":"Make $y$ the subject of $3x+2y=14$.","options":["$y=14-3x$","$y=\\dfrac{14-3x}{2}$","$y=\\dfrac{3x-14}{2}$","$y=7-3x$"],"correct":1,"explain":"Subtract $3x$: $2y=14-3x$. Then divide the **whole** right side by 2."},{"q":"Solve $3(2x-1)=15$.","options":["$x=2$","$x=4$","$x=3$","$x=9$"],"correct":2,"explain":"Divide by 3: $2x-1=5$, so $2x=6$ and $x=3$."},{"q":"Solve $\\dfrac{x}{3}+2=5$.","options":["$x=9$","$x=1$","$x=15$","$x=7$"],"correct":0,"explain":"Subtract 2: $\\dfrac{x}{3}=3$. Multiply by 3: $x=9$."},{"q":"If $-4x<12$, then","options":["$x<-3$","$x>3$","$x\\leq-3$","$x>-3$"],"correct":3,"explain":"Divide by $-4$ and reverse the sign: $x>-3$."},{"q":"Which inequality means “at least 12 learners”?","options":["$n<12$","$n\\geq12$","$n\\leq12$","$n>12$"],"correct":1,"explain":"“At least 12” means 12 or more."},{"q":"Solve $x+y=9$ and $x-y=3$.","options":["$x=3,\\ y=6$","$x=5,\\ y=4$","$x=6,\\ y=3$","$x=9,\\ y=3$"],"correct":2,"explain":"Adding gives $2x=12$, so $x=6$ and $y=3$."},{"q":"The formula $A=\\tfrac{1}{2}bh$, rearranged for $h$, is","options":["$h=\\dfrac{2A}{b}$","$h=\\dfrac{A}{2b}$","$h=\\dfrac{b}{2A}$","$h=2Ab$"],"correct":0,"explain":"Multiply by 2: $2A=bh$. Divide by $b$: $h=\\dfrac{2A}{b}$."},{"q":"Which inequality is shown with a filled circle at its endpoint?","options":["$x>4$","$x<4$","$x\\neq4$","$x\\leq4$"],"correct":3,"explain":"The “equals” part of $\\leq$ means the endpoint is included, so the circle is filled."},{"q":"Solve $5-2x\\geq11$.","options":["$x\\geq-3$","$x\\leq-3$","$x\\leq3$","$x>-3$"],"correct":1,"explain":"$-2x\\geq6$. Dividing by $-2$ reverses the sign: $x\\leq-3$."},{"q":"A taxi fare is GH₵5 plus GH₵2 per kilometre. Which formula gives the fare $C$ (in cedis) for $d$ km?","options":["$C=2+5d$","$C=10d$","$C=5+2d$","$C=5d+2d$"],"correct":2,"explain":"A fixed charge of 5 plus 2 for each kilometre."}],"exercise":[{"q":"Make $r$ the subject of $3c+2r=md+k$.","a":"$r=\\dfrac{md+k-3c}{2}$"},{"q":"Solve $4(3x-5)-2(x+1)=3x+6$.","a":"$10x-22=3x+6$, so $7x=28$ and $x=4$."},{"q":"Solve $\\dfrac{x-1}{4}+\\dfrac{x+2}{3}=5$.","a":"Multiply by 12: $3(x-1)+4(x+2)=60$, so $7x+5=60$ and $x=\\dfrac{55}{7}=7\\dfrac{6}{7}$."},{"q":"A school pays GH₵960 for 50 books and calculators. Books cost GH₵12 and calculators GH₵24. How many of each did it buy?","a":"$b+c=50$ and $12b+24c=960$ (so $b+2c=80$): $c=30$ calculators and $b=20$ books."},{"q":"Solve $7-2(3x+1)<3x+14$ and describe the number line.","a":"$5-6x<3x+14$, so $-9x<9$ and $x>-1$: an open circle at $-1$, shaded to the right."},{"q":"Make $x$ the subject of $y=\\dfrac{3x-2}{5}$.","a":"$5y=3x-2$, so $x=\\dfrac{5y+2}{3}$."},{"q":"Solve by substitution: $y=2x-1$ and $3x+2y=12$.","a":"$3x+2(2x-1)=12$, so $7x=14$: $x=2$, $y=3$."},{"q":"Solve $-3<2x+1\\leq7$ and list the integers that satisfy it.","a":"$-4<2x\\leq6$, so $-2<x\\leq3$. Integers: $-1,\\ 0,\\ 1,\\ 2,\\ 3$."}],"theory":[{"q":"The period of a pendulum is $T=2\\pi\\sqrt{\\dfrac{L}{g}}$. Make $g$ the subject (all quantities are positive).","steps":["Divide by $2\\pi$: $\\dfrac{T}{2\\pi}=\\sqrt{\\dfrac{L}{g}}$.","Square both sides: $\\dfrac{T^2}{4\\pi^2}=\\dfrac{L}{g}$.","Multiply both sides by $4\\pi^2g$, then divide by $T^2$."],"answer":"$g=\\dfrac{4\\pi^2L}{T^2}$","model":null},{"q":"Solve $3(2x+5)-4(x-1)=7x-6$.","steps":["Expand: $6x+15-4x+4=7x-6$.","Simplify: $2x+19=7x-6$.","Add 6 and subtract $2x$: $25=5x$.","Check: $3(15)-4(4)=29$ and $7(5)-6=29$ ✓."],"answer":"$x=5$","model":null},{"q":"Solve the simultaneous equations $3x+2y=19$ and $2x-y=1$.","steps":["Multiply the second equation by 2: $4x-2y=2$.","Add to the first: $7x=21$, so $x=3$.","Substitute: $2(3)-y=1$, so $y=5$.","Check in the first equation: $9+10=19$ ✓."],"answer":"$x=3$, $y=5$","model":null},{"q":"Solve $2-\\dfrac{3x-1}{4}\\leq\\dfrac{x+5}{2}$.","steps":["Multiply every term by 4 (positive): $8-(3x-1)\\leq2(x+5)$.","Expand: $9-3x\\leq2x+10$.","Add $3x$ and subtract 10: $-1\\leq5x$.","Divide by 5: $x\\geq-\\dfrac{1}{5}$ (a filled circle at $-\\dfrac{1}{5}$, shaded to the right)."],"answer":"$x\\geq-\\dfrac{1}{5}$","model":null},{"q":"A bus can carry no more than 75 passengers and already has 18 on board. Groups of 7 passengers are waiting. What is the largest number of whole groups it can still take?","steps":["Let $g$ be the number of groups (a whole number, $g\\geq0$).","$18+7g\\leq75$, so $7g\\leq57$ and $g\\leq\\dfrac{57}{7}\\approx8.14$.","$g$ must be a whole number, so the largest value is $8$.","Check: $18+7\\times8=74\\leq75$, but $18+7\\times9=81>75$."],"answer":"8 groups","model":null}],"checklist":["I can tell the difference between an expression, an equation and a formula.","I can change the subject of a formula, including one with a square or square root.","I can solve equations with brackets and fractions, and check my answer.","I can solve simultaneous equations by elimination and by substitution.","I can solve inequalities, reversing the sign when I multiply or divide by a negative.","I can show a solution set on a number line with open and filled circles."],"plan":{"lessons":[[{"j":0,"notes":true,"exs":[]},{"j":1,"notes":true,"exs":[]},{"j":2,"notes":true,"exs":[0,1]},{"j":3,"notes":true,"exs":[2]},{"j":4,"notes":true,"exs":[3]}],[{"j":5,"notes":true,"exs":[4]},{"j":6,"notes":true,"exs":[]},{"j":7,"notes":true,"exs":[5,6,7]},{"j":8,"notes":true,"exs":[]}]],"exSec":[2,2,3,4,5,7,7,7],"quizSec":[2,7,7,7,7,7,2,7,7,2],"exerSec":[2,7,7,0,7,2,5,7],"thSec":[2,7,5,7,6],"sumSec":[2,4,5,7,7],"chkSec":[0,2,3,5,7,7],"weights":[305.35,732.65,2013.7,944.3,1213.6,1591.6,459.85,3245.3,267.4],"figs":[{"id":"w11-balance","sec":1,"lesson":1,"caption":"$3x+7=25$: remove 7 from both pans, then share each pan into 3 equal parts, to find $x=6$."},{"id":"w11-lines","sec":5,"lesson":2,"caption":"Each equation is a straight line. <script type="application/json" id="pack-y1w12">{"year":1,"week":12,"id":"y1w12","title":"Relations, Functions and Mapping Rules","subtitle":"Ordered pairs, mapping diagrams, tables and graphs; domain, co-domain and range; types of relations; functions and the vertical line test; linear and exponential mapping rules.","family":"algebra","section":{"no":2,"name":"Algebra","strand":"Algebraic Reasoning","from":9,"to":12},"outcomes":["Represent a relation as ordered pairs, a mapping diagram, a table and a graph.","Identify the domain, co-domain and range of a relation.","Classify relations as one-to-one, many-to-one, one-to-many or many-to-many, and decide whether a relation is a function.","Evaluate functions and find linear rules from points or tables.","Recognise and use simple exponential mapping rules."],"keywords":["relation","ordered pair","mapping diagram","domain","co-domain","range","function","one-to-one","many-to-one","vertical line test","gradient","exponential"],"notes":[{"title":"What is a relation?","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A **relation** connects elements of one set (the inputs) to elements of another set (the outputs). We can show it as **ordered pairs** $(\\text{input},\\ \\text{output})$, an arrow (mapping) diagram, a table, a graph or a rule. Order matters: $(2,5)$ is not the same as $(5,2)$."},{"k":"box","kind":"definition","title":"Domain, co-domain and range","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["The **domain** is the set of inputs.","The **co-domain** is the set of possible outputs that has been declared.","The **range** is the set of outputs actually reached. The range is a subset of the co-domain."]}]},{"k":"p","text":"For $R=\\{(1,2),\\ (2,4),\\ (3,6)\\}$: the domain is $\\{1,2,3\\}$ and the range is $\\{2,4,6\\}$."},{"k":"fig","id":"w12-domain","caption":"The co-domain is $\\{2,4,6,8,10\\}$, but only $2,4,6,8$ receive arrows, so the range is $\\{2,4,6,8\\}$."}],"figs":["w12-domain"]},{"title":"Types of relations","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["**One-to-one:** each input has one output, and different inputs have different outputs.","**Many-to-one:** each input has one output, but some inputs share an output.","**One-to-many:** at least one input has more than one output.","**Many-to-many:** several inputs share outputs **and** some inputs have more than one output."]},{"k":"fig","id":"w12-types","caption":"One-to-one and many-to-one relations are functions. One-to-many and many-to-many relations are not, because an input has more than one output."}],"figs":["w12-types"]},{"title":"Functions","blocks":[{"k":"box","kind":"definition","title":"Function","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A **function** is a relation in which **every** input in the domain has **exactly one** output."}]},{"k":"p","text":"Two different inputs may give the same output (many-to-one is allowed), but one input may never give two different outputs."},{"k":"p","text":"We often write a function as $f(x)$, read “$f$ of $x$”. For $f(x)=2x+1$:"},{"k":"math","tex":"f(3)=2(3)+1=7"},{"k":"p","text":"The output $7$ is called the **image** of $3$, and we can write $3\\mapsto7$."},{"k":"box","kind":"key","title":"The vertical line test","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A graph shows $y$ as a function of $x$ if **no vertical line** cuts it more than once. A circle fails the test; a straight line that is not vertical passes it."}]},{"k":"fig","id":"w12-vlt","caption":"The parabola $y=x^2$ passes the vertical line test; the circle does not."}],"figs":["w12-vlt"]},{"title":"Mapping diagrams","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Draw two ovals: the domain on the left and the co-domain on the right. Draw one arrow from each input to its output."},{"k":"ul","items":["For a function, every input has **exactly one** arrow.","An element of the co-domain may receive no arrow, or several arrows."]}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Evaluating functions and inverse relations","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"To evaluate $f(-2)$, replace **every** $x$ by $(-2)$, using brackets:"},{"k":"math","tex":"f(x)=x^2-3x\\quad\\Longrightarrow\\quad f(-2)=(-2)^2-3(-2)=4+6=10"},{"k":"box","kind":"warn","title":"Use brackets for negative inputs","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"$(-2)^2=4$, but $-2^2=-4$. Always put a negative input in brackets."}]},{"k":"p","text":"The **inverse relation** swaps the coordinates of every ordered pair. The inverse of a function is **not always** a function: if two inputs share an output, the inverse gives that output two images."}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Linear mapping rules","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A **linear** rule $y=mx+c$ has a constant rate of change: when the inputs go up in equal steps, the outputs change by equal amounts."},{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"Finding a linear rule from two points","blocks":[{"k":"math","tex":"m=\\frac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}\\qquad(x_2\\neq x_1)"},{"k":"p","text":"Then substitute one point into $y=mx+c$ to find $c$."}]},{"k":"p","text":"The $y$-intercept of $y=mx+c$ is $(0,c)$. In real situations it is often a starting value, such as a fixed fee."}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Exponential mapping rules","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"An **exponential** rule multiplies the output by the same number (the **common ratio**) each time the input goes up by 1:"},{"k":"math","tex":"y=a\\,r^{x}"},{"k":"p","text":"Here $a$ is the value when $x=0$ and $r$ is the common ratio. For $y=3(2^x)$: $x=0,1,2,3$ gives $y=3,6,12,24$."},{"k":"fig","id":"w12-linexp","caption":"The linear rule adds the same amount each step; the exponential rule multiplies by the same amount, so it grows faster and faster."},{"k":"box","kind":"tip","title":"Difference or ratio?","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Look at the outputs for equally spaced inputs."},{"k":"ul","items":["Constant **difference** ($3,6,9,12$: add 3) means linear.","Constant **ratio** ($3,6,12,24$: multiply by 2) means exponential."]}]}],"figs":["w12-linexp"]},{"title":"Graphs and modelling","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Plot $(x,y)$ by moving $x$ units across and then $y$ units up or down. gradient","options":["$2$","$-2$","$\\dfrac{1}{2}$","$-\\dfrac{1}{2}$"],"correct":1,"explain":"Rearrange: $2y=-4x+7$, so $y=-2x+\\dfrac{7}{2}$ and $m=-2$."},{"q":"A line perpendicular to a line of gradient $-\\dfrac{5}{2}$ has gradient","options":["$-\\dfrac{2}{5}$","$\\dfrac{2}{5}$","$\\dfrac{5}{2}$","$-\\dfrac{5}{2}$"],"correct":1,"explain":"Perpendicular gradients multiply to $-1$: $-\\dfrac{5}{2}\\times\\dfrac{2}{5}=-1$."},{"q":"Which point lies on $y=2x+1$?","options":["$(2,4)$","$(1,1)$","$(-1,-1)$","$(0,2)$"],"correct":2,"explain":"When $x=-1$, $y=2(-1)+1=-1$. The other points do not satisfy the equation."},{"q":"The $x$-intercept of $3x+2y=12$ is","options":["$(0,6)$","$(6,0)$","$(0,4)$","$(4,0)$"],"correct":3,"explain":"Put $y=0$: $3x=12$, so $x=4$. The intercept is the point $(4,0)$."},{"q":"The horizontal line through $(3,7)$ has equation","options":["$x=3$","$y=7$","$y=3$","$x=7$"],"correct":1,"explain":"Every point on a horizontal line has the same $y$-coordinate, here $7$."},{"q":"A taxi charges GH₵10 plus GH₵4 per kilometre. How far did a learner travel if the fare was GH₵43?","a":"$8+2.5d=43$, so $2.5d=35$ and $d=14$ km."},{"q":"A line through $(k,2)$ and $(4,8)$ has gradient $2$. Show that the three points lie on one straight line, and find the equation of that line.","steps":["Gradient of $PQ$: $m_{PQ}=\\dfrac{3-(-3)}{1-(-2)}=\\dfrac{6}{3}=2$.","Gradient of $QR$: $m_{QR}=\\dfrac{9-3}{4-1}=\\dfrac{6}{3}=2$.","The gradients are equal and the segments share the point $Q$, so $P$, $Q$ and $R$ are collinear.","Using $Q(1,3)$: $y-3=2(x-1)$, so $y=2x+1$.","Check: $2(-2)+1=-3$ for $P$ and $2(4)+1=9$ for $R$."],"answer":"The points are collinear; the line is $y=2x+1$.","model":null},{"q":"Find the equation of the line through $(3,-2)$ that is perpendicular to $2x+5y-10=0$. After 2 minutes it holds 340 litres; after 7 minutes it holds 190 litres. Find $x$, each angle, and an angle co-interior with one of them.","steps":["Corresponding angles between parallel lines are equal: $3x+15=5x-25$.","$2x=40$, so $x=20$.","Each angle is $3(20)+15=75^\\circ$; check: $5(20)-25=75^\\circ$ ✓.","Co-interior angles add up to $180^\\circ$: $180^\\circ-75^\\circ=105^\\circ$."],"answer":"$x=20$; each angle is $75^\\circ$; the co-interior angle is $105^\\circ$.","model":null},{"q":"The supplement of an angle is four times its complement. Find $x$, list the angles and classify each.","steps":["Angles at a point: $x+2x+(3x-20)+(x+30)=360$.","$7x+10=360$, so $x=50$.","The angles are $50^\\circ$, $100^\\circ$, $130^\\circ$ and $80^\\circ$ (sum $360^\\circ$ ✓).","$50^\\circ$ and $80^\\circ$ are acute; $100^\\circ$ and $130^\\circ$ are obtuse."],"answer":"$x=50$; $50^\\circ$, $100^\\circ$, $130^\\circ$, $80^\\circ$","model":null},{"q":"Describe how to construct angles of $60^\\circ$ and $30^\\circ$ with only a ruler and compasses, and explain why the method works.","steps":["Draw a ray $OA$. Join $OQ$.","$OP$, $OQ$ and $PQ$ are all equal to the radius, so triangle $OPQ$ is equilateral and $\\angle QOP=60^\\circ$.","Bisect $\\angle QOP$: equal arcs from $P$ and $Q$ meet at $R$; join $OR$. Then $\\angle ROP=30^\\circ$."],"answer":"An equilateral triangle gives $60^\\circ$; bisecting it gives $30^\\circ$.","model":null},{"q":"Find the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at (a) 4:00 (b) 2:30. solve problems on the Pythagorean theorem, parallel lines, perpendicular lines and transversals; use the exterior angle theorem and calculate the sums of the interior and exterior angles of polygons."],"indicators":["Draw and describe angles with various measures, including acute, right, straight, obtuse and reflex angles.","Solve problems that involve parallel lines, perpendicular lines and transversals, and pairs of angles formed between them."],"focal":[],"exemplars":["Review learners’ JHS knowledge of angles and discuss referents for angles.","In mixed groups, learners explore the school and classroom surroundings for referents of angles.","Learners sketch angles freehand, estimate their sizes, then check with a protractor.","In small groups, learners bisect angles, then discuss the types of angle.","Think-pair-share: learners solve problems on pairs of angles.","Whole-class discussion of parallel lines, perpendicular lines and transversals.","Mixed-ability groups work through task sheets on the angles formed by a transversal."],"flags":[],"source":"tm","assess":[]},"figImgs":{"w14-types":{"png":"
